raw: {"need": "Competence", "secondary": {"name": "Identity"}, "read": "Going quiet and doing the minimum is almost never laziness. It usually means they have decided at some level that trying and falling short is more dangerous to how they see themselves than simply not trying. The bare minimum is a controlled outcome. If they never fully engage, they never fully fail. There is also an identity question underneath: they may not yet see this work as connected to who they are becoming, which makes it easy to treat as something to get through rather than something to get good at.", "pull": {"collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Let it ride and hope they come around on their own, because pushing someone who is already withdrawn feels like it will make things worse and create an awkward dynamic."}, "mentorMove": "Go to them before the silence becomes the norm. Name what you are seeing without judgment, get genuinely curious about what is getting in the way, and connect the work to something they actually care about being or becoming.", "holdFirm": ["The standard of work does not drop because they are going through something.", "They stay in the conversation about how to get there, not out of it."], "stayFlexible": ["What the path back to full engagement looks like and at what pace.", "Which part of the work they can lean into first to rebuild momentum."], "forceLevel": {"level": 2, "label": "Questions"}, "script": [{"phase": "Connection", "words": "I have noticed you have been pretty quiet lately and keeping things at arm's length. I am not here to put you on the spot. I just do not want to let it sit there without checking in."}, {"phase": "Curiosity", "words": "What is going on for you right now? Not a performance review, just a real question. Is it the work itself, something about the situation here, something outside of work? I would rather know than guess."}, {"phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Tell me what part of this job, if any, actually interests you or connects to where you want to be in a few years. I am asking because I want to figure out how to make the work worth putting real effort into, not just worth showing up for."}, {"phase": "Commitment", "words": "Here is what I need from you going forward: full effort, not perfection. I am holding you to that because I think you have more in you than what I have been seeing, and I would rather say that directly than watch you stay smaller than you are."}], "longGame": "The habit you are building in them is learning to stay in the room when things feel uncertain rather than shrinking down to minimum safe output. People who can stay engaged when they are not sure they will succeed are the ones who actually develop. That is the capacity worth going after here."}
situation: Someone I am responsible for has gone quiet and is doing the bare minimum.
